scenarios.title: The Empty Peg
text: His best mate at the club has been sold. The peg next to his is empty, a strip of tape still showing the name. The group chat is quieter already.
The transfer happened in a day. One minute they were laughing in the canteen, the next his friend was posting a photo in a new shirt. {J} found out from the internet.
scenarios.prompt: Your closest teammate has left the club.

choices.label: Drive him to the airport
choices.text: They sit in the car outside departures for twenty minutes, saying very little. 'Same group chat,' says his friend. 'Always.'

choices.label: Throw himself into training
choices.text: He trains harder than anyone for a week. The coaches love it. He's lonely at lunch.

choices.label: Make an effort with someone new
choices.desc: The squad is bigger than one man.
choices.text: He sits with {T} at lunch for the first time. It turns out they have the same terrible taste in music.

scenarios.title: The New Boy
text: {T} arrived this week from abroad. He doesn't speak the language, doesn't know where the canteen is, and ate lunch alone in his car today.
The new signing, {T}, is clearly struggling: lost in drills, quiet in meetings, homesick in every photo he posts.
scenarios.prompt: A new teammate is struggling to settle.

choices.label: Take him under your wing
choices.text: He shows {T} where to eat, where to live and which coach to avoid. By the end of the month {T} is laughing in the canteen.

choices.label: Leave it to the club
choices.text: The welfare officer does their job. {T} settles slowly. He never quite forgets who didn't help.

scenarios.title: The Kid Who Reminds Him of Himself
scenarios.text: A seventeen-year-old has been promoted from the academy: same position, same nerves, same way of staring at the senior players like they're gods. It's like looking in a mirror from years ago.
scenarios.prompt: A young academy graduate plays your position.

choices.label: Mentor him properly
choices.desc: Everything you wish someone had taught you.
choices.hint: One day he might take your place. That's the point.
choices.text: Extra sessions, honest advice, a phone number for the bad days. The kid improves fast. One day he'll take the shirt; {J} hopes he does.

choices.label: Make him earn it
choices.text: He goes hard in every drill against the kid. The kid gets better, and a little scared.

choices.label: Keep him at a distance
choices.text: He keeps the kid at arm's length. The senior players notice. So does the kid.

scenarios.title: {T}'s Wedding
scenarios.text: {T} is getting married and wants {J} to give a speech at the reception. In front of four hundred people. In two languages.
scenarios.prompt: Give the wedding speech?

choices.label: Yes, and make them laugh
choices.hint: A great speech is remembered forever.

out.text: The speech is a triumph: two embarrassing stories, one touching line, and a toast in {T}'s mother's language. {T} hugs him for a full minute.
He freezes halfway through. {T}'s grandmother finishes the toast for him. Everyone thinks it's adorable.

choices.label: Politely say you're not a speaker
choices.desc: Offer to organise the stag do instead.
choices.text: He organises a legendary stag weekend instead. {T} says it was even better than a speech.

scenarios.title: {T} Is a Dad
scenarios.text: {T}'s first child was born at 4am. He's at training at 10, eyes red, grinning like an idiot, showing everyone the same eleven photos.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate has just become a father.

choices.label: Organise a squad gift
choices.desc: A collection, a card, a tiny shirt.
choices.text: A tiny shirt with the baby's name and number 1, signed by the whole squad. {T} cries in the dressing room. Nobody teases him.

choices.label: Congratulate him and move on
choices.text: A warm handshake and a 'congrats, man'. {T} is too tired to remember who said what anyway.

scenarios.title: {T}'s Father
scenarios.text: {T}'s father died suddenly yesterday. He's flying home tonight. He came to the training ground to collect his boots and is sitting alone in his car in the car park.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate has lost his father.

choices.label: Sit with him in the car
choices.text: He sits in the passenger seat for half an hour. They don't say much. When {T} drives away, he raises a hand from the window.

choices.label: Organise the squad to wear black armbands
choices.desc: A tribute at the next match.
choices.hint: A gesture the family will see.
choices.text: The whole squad wears black armbands at the weekend. {T}'s family watches on TV back home and writes the club a letter.

scenarios.title: The Captain Is Retiring
scenarios.text: {CAP} announces he'll retire at the end of the season. In the dressing room afterwards, he looks around the room and his eyes stop on {J} for a moment.
scenarios.prompt: The captain is leaving. The armband will need a new home.

choices.label: Tell {CAPl} you'd like to be considered

ok.text: {CAPl} nods slowly. 'I already told the manager it should be you.' At the start of next season, the armband is his.

bad.text: {CAPl} says he's recommended someone else. 'Your time will come.'

choices.label: Say nothing, keep leading by example
choices.text: He keeps his head down and his standards high. The decision will come in its own time.

scenarios.title: One Shirt, Two Players
text: The manager has been rotating {J} and {T} week to week. Neither of them is happy. In the gym, they don't make eye contact.
{T} plays your position and has started the last three matches. You've been on the bench for all three.
scenarios.prompt: You're fighting {T} for a place.

choices.label: Make it a friendly rivalry
choices.text: They start a running competition in training: whoever loses buys coffee. Both improve. The manager has a happy headache.

choices.label: Go to the manager for answers

out.text: 'You are,' says {Mf}. 'But keep pushing.' {J} walks out ten feet tall.
'Right now, {Tl} is,' says {Mf}. At least he knows.

choices.label: Freeze {T} out
choices.text: They stop speaking. The dressing room tension becomes a story in the papers.

scenarios.title: The FIFA Tournament
scenarios.text: The squad has a video-game tournament every international break. The trophy is a plastic cup with a toy footballer glued to it. {T} has won it four times running and won't stop talking about it.
scenarios.prompt: Enter the squad tournament?

out.text: He beats {T} in the final on penalties. The squad goes wild. The plastic cup has pride of place on his shelf.
Knocked out in the first round by the reserve goalkeeper. The squad will never let him forget it.

choices.label: Commentate instead
choices.text: His live commentary of the final becomes legendary. Someone films it. The club posts it.

scenarios.title: Breaking the Fast
scenarios.text: It's Ramadan. {T} and several teammates are fasting through training. The club has arranged a late iftar at the training ground and invited the whole squad.
scenarios.prompt: Join the squad iftar?

choices.label: Join, whatever your faith
choices.text: Dates, soup, a long table and a lot of laughter. The fasting players are touched that everyone came.

choices.label: Help organise it
choices.text: He helps organise the iftar every week of Ramadan. The squad has never been closer.

scenarios.title: Every Night Is a Party
scenarios.text: {T} is out every night: clubs, yachts, rooftop bars. He keeps inviting {J}. His form has dropped off a cliff, and the manager is watching both of them.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate's lifestyle is pulling you in.

choices.label: Decline, every time
choices.text: He declines so often that {T} stops asking. His fitness numbers are the best in the squad.

choices.label: Go once a month
choices.text: Once a month, never before a match. He has a good time and a clear head.

out.text: {T} laughs it off. Then, a month later, he cuts down. He thanks {J} at the end of the season.
{T} tells him he's boring. They drift apart.

scenarios.title: {T} Knows Everything
scenarios.text: {T} knows every secret in the club: who's being sold, whose marriage is in trouble, what the manager said about whom. Today he leans in: 'You want to know what {Mf} really thinks of you?'
scenarios.prompt: Listen to the gossip?

out.text: Apparently {Mf} rates him highly but thinks he's lazy without the ball. Useful, painful, true.
Apparently {Mf} said something cruel. It may not even be true. It sits in his head for weeks.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: He walks away. {T} shrugs and tells someone else. He's happier not knowing.

scenarios.title: Lessons From the Old Man
scenarios.text: {T}, the oldest player in the squad, takes {J} for coffee and says, 'Let me tell you what I wish someone had told me at your age.' He has been in football for seventeen years.
scenarios.prompt: What do you ask the veteran?

choices.label: About money
choices.desc: How not to end up broke.
choices.hint: The most useful conversation of your career.
choices.text: {T} talks about the teammates who ended up broke: cars, friends, bad advice. He gives {J} the name of an honest financial adviser.

choices.label: About surviving managers
choices.text: 'Every manager wants three things: effort, honesty and no surprises.' {J} writes it in his notes app.

choices.label: About family
choices.text: {T} talks about the birthdays he missed and the divorce he didn't see coming. {J} calls home that night.

scenarios.title: Cake Ambush
scenarios.text: It's {T}'s birthday. The squad tradition is to ambush the birthday boy with a cake to the face after training. Somebody has to carry the cake.
scenarios.prompt: Carry the cake?

choices.label: Carry it, and do it properly
choices.text: Perfect execution. {T} is covered in icing and laughing. The video is the club's most-watched post of the month.

choices.label: Film it
choices.text: He films it. The footage is shaky because he's laughing too hard.

scenarios.title: The Dressing-Room Awards
scenarios.text: End-of-season dressing-room awards: Worst Dressed, Most Likely to Be Late, Best Moaner. The voting is secret and brutal. {J} has been nominated for three.
scenarios.prompt: How do you take it?

choices.label: Accept every award with a speech
choices.text: He accepts 'Worst Dressed' wearing the outfit in question. Standing ovation.

choices.label: Demand a recount
choices.text: His demand for a recount is so dramatic that the squad invents a new award just for him: Worst Loser.

scenarios.title: Wages
scenarios.text: Someone leaked the squad's wages. {J} earns more than {T}, who has been at the club for six years. {T} hasn't said anything. His face says everything.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate resents your wage.

choices.label: Talk to him honestly
choices.text: {T} admits he's hurt, but not at {J}. They end up going to the board together to push for better deals for the long-serving players.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: Nothing is said. Something changes.

scenarios.title: Not Okay
scenarios.text: In the dressing room, a senior player makes a 'joke' about {T}'s skin colour. A few people laugh. {T} doesn't. He stares at the floor.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate was racially mocked.

choices.label: Call it out, right there
choices.text: 'That's not funny, and it's not okay.' The room goes silent. The senior player mumbles an apology. {T} catches {J}'s eye and nods.

choices.label: Talk to {T} privately afterwards
choices.desc: Check he's okay. Ask what he wants.
choices.text: {T} says it happens more than people know. Together they go to the captain. It doesn't happen again.

scenarios.title: {T}'s Car
scenarios.text: {T} crashed his sports car into a lamppost at 2am. He's fine, mostly. The police are involved. The manager is livid. {T} calls {J} from the station.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate is in trouble and called you.

choices.label: Go and get him
choices.text: He picks {T} up at 4am and drives him home. On the way {T} admits he'd been drinking. They sit in the car outside his flat until the sun comes up.

choices.label: Call the club's lawyer for him
choices.text: The club lawyer arrives in twenty minutes. {T} is grateful. The newspapers still get the story.

scenarios.title: Caught in the Middle
scenarios.text: {T} and {T2} haven't spoken in a month. Both of them are friends with {J}. Both have asked him, separately, whose side he's on.
scenarios.prompt: Two teammates want you to pick a side.

choices.label: Get them in a room together

out.text: Pizza, a locked door and two hours. They come out laughing. The squad can't believe it.
It explodes. Now both of them are angry at {J}.

choices.label: Refuse to choose
choices.text: He refuses to pick a side. Both respect it, grudgingly.

choices.label: Side with {T}
choices.hint: A friend kept, a friend lost.
choices.text: He backs {T}. {T2} takes it personally.

scenarios.title: The Charity Match
scenarios.text: The squad is playing a charity match against a team of local celebrities and retired legends. Nobody is supposed to try too hard. Somebody always does.
scenarios.prompt: How seriously do you take it?

choices.label: Entertain: tricks, jokes, let the celebrities score
choices.text: He lets a famous comedian nutmeg him and falls over dramatically. The crowd loves it. The charity raises a fortune.

choices.label: Play properly
choices.text: He scores a hat-trick against retired men in their fifties. Technically impressive, socially questionable.

scenarios.title: The Investment
scenarios.text: {T} is pitching every player in the squad on a business: a chain of padel courts. He wants {J} in for a slice. 'Can't lose,' he says, which is always what people say.
scenarios.prompt: Invest in a teammate's business?

choices.label: Invest a little
choices.hint: Money might come back. Might not.

out.text: The padel courts are packed. A year later he gets a cheque bigger than his investment.
The business folds in eight months. {T} apologises every time they see each other.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: He declines kindly. {T} understands. Mostly.

scenarios.title: The Captain Notices
scenarios.text: {CAP} catches {J} staring at his phone in the physio room for twenty minutes. 'Trouble at home?' he asks. It isn't really a question.
scenarios.prompt: The captain offers to listen.

choices.label: Open up
choices.text: {CAPl} listens, then says, 'I nearly lost my wife over football. Go home on time tonight. Every night this week.' {J} does.

choices.label: Say it's nothing
choices.text: 'Nothing, captain.' {CAPl} nods and leaves the door open anyway.

scenarios.title: {FORMER} on the Other Side
scenarios.text: {FORMER}, his old friend from {FORMERCLUB}, is playing against him this weekend. They text all week. Trash talk, mostly. Some of it serious.
scenarios.prompt: Your old friend is in the other team.

choices.label: Swap shirts after the match
choices.text: They swap shirts on the halfway line at full time and hug for a long time. The photo goes everywhere.

choices.label: Promise to nutmeg him
choices.text: He does nutmeg him, in the 34th minute. {FORMER} laughs so hard he nearly falls over.

scenarios.title: {T} Comes Back
scenarios.text: {T} has been out for nine months with a knee injury. Today is his first full session back. He's nervous. Everyone is being careful around him.
scenarios.prompt: Help a teammate's comeback?

choices.label: Train with him, no special treatment
choices.text: He tackles {T} in the first drill, fairly and firmly. {T} grins: 'Thank you. I needed that.'

choices.label: Ask him how the rehab really was
choices.text: {T} talks for an hour about the loneliness of the gym. {J} remembers it if his own knee ever goes.

scenarios.title: Come With Me
scenarios.text: {T} has an offer from a big club, and the club wants a second player in his position. He's recommended {J}. 'Come with me,' he says. 'We'll do it together.'
scenarios.prompt: Your friend wants you to move with him.

choices.label: Tell your agent to look into it
choices.text: His agent makes calls. An offer comes within weeks, from the same club.

choices.label: Stay
choices.text: {T} goes alone. They stay friends. {J} wonders, sometimes.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Job
scenarios.text: Being captain is more than the armband. A young player wants to talk about homesickness, two seniors are feuding, and the kit man has asked {J} to sort out the coffee machine.
scenarios.prompt: What do you prioritise as captain?

choices.label: The young player first
choices.hint: The squad notices who you look after.
choices.text: He spends an evening with the homesick kid and his family on video. The kid settles. The squad sees.

choices.label: The feud first
choices.text: He sits the two seniors down and sorts it. It takes three hours and all his patience.

choices.label: The coffee machine, obviously
choices.text: He buys a new coffee machine with his own money. Honestly, the most popular thing he does all season.

scenarios.title: The Back Seat
scenarios.text: First away trip. He sits on the back seat of the team bus. Nobody says anything. Then {CAP} gets on, looks at him, and waits.
scenarios.prompt: You're in the captain's seat.

choices.label: Move immediately with an apology
choices.text: He moves so fast he trips. {CAPl} laughs and pats his head. Lesson learned, gently.

choices.label: Stay put with a cheeky grin

out.text: {CAPl} grins back and sits next to him. 'I like this kid.'
{CAPl} doesn't grin. {J} carries the kit bags for a month.

scenarios.title: {T} Trusts Him
scenarios.text: {T} asks {J} to stay behind after training. Haltingly, he tells him he's gay, and that he's thinking about telling the squad. He's terrified. He wanted {J} to know first.
scenarios.prompt: Your friend has trusted you with something important.

choices.label: Promise to stand with him, whatever he decides
choices.text: 'Whatever you decide, I'm next to you.' {T} lets out a breath he's been holding for years.

choices.label: Help him plan how to tell the squad
choices.text: They plan it together, with the captain. When {T} tells the squad, {J} is the first to hug him. The room follows.

scenarios.title: His Childhood Hero
scenarios.text: The opposition includes a veteran {J} worshipped as a kid: posters on the wall, his name on a homemade shirt. After the match, {J} is too shy to ask for his shirt.
scenarios.prompt: Ask your childhood hero for his shirt?

choices.label: Ask
choices.desc: You'll regret it if you don't.
choices.text: The veteran laughs and says he was going to ask for {J}'s. They swap. The shirt is framed above his bed within the week.

choices.label: Don't
choices.text: He doesn't ask. He thinks about it on the bus home, and for years afterwards.

scenarios.title: The Kid in Trouble
scenarios.text: One of the youngsters, {T}, has been seen with the wrong crowd: expensive cars, men who don't work, a lot of cash. He's nineteen. He reminds {J} of someone.
scenarios.prompt: A young teammate is heading down a bad road.

out.text: {T} gets defensive, then quiet, then tells him everything. With {J}'s help, he walks away from them.
{T} tells him to mind his business. Six months later, the headlines arrive.

choices.label: Tell the club's welfare team
choices.text: The welfare team steps in quietly. {T} doesn't know who raised it. He's okay, in the end.

scenarios.title: The Ritual
scenarios.text: Every player has a pre-match ritual: left boot first, the same song, a prayer, touching the badge on the tunnel wall. {J} has been asked what his is for a club video. He doesn't have one. Yet.
scenarios.prompt: What becomes your ritual?

choices.label: A message to {MUM} before every match
choices.text: Three words to {MUM}, every match. She replies with a heart within seconds, always.

choices.label: Touch the badge on the tunnel wall
choices.text: He touches the badge every time. The fans start doing it too, at the turnstiles.

choices.label: Something nobody knows about
choices.text: He tells the camera it's a secret. The video goes viral with fans guessing.

scenarios.title: Day Off Together
scenarios.text: The squad has two days off and someone suggests going away together: a beach, a rented house, twenty footballers and one barbecue.
scenarios.prompt: Go on the squad trip?

choices.label: Go
choices.text: Two days of beach football, terrible singing and burnt sausages. The team that comes back is closer.

choices.label: Stay home with family
choices.text: He goes home instead. {MUM} is thrilled. The squad photos look fun.

scenarios.title: Say Something, Kid
scenarios.text: Before a big match, the captain does something unusual: he asks the youngest player to say a few words. That's {J}. Twenty-five grown men turn to look at him.
scenarios.prompt: The captain wants you to speak.

choices.label: Speak from the heart
choices.desc: Say what this means to you.

ok.text: He talks about watching this club from the cheap seats with his dad. The room goes very quiet. Then they roar.

bad.text: He says 'let's win' and sits down. Somebody claps, kindly.

choices.label: Make them laugh
choices.text: One joke about the captain's haircut. The whole room breaks up. They go out loose and laughing.

scenarios.title: What He Saw
scenarios.text: {J} saw {T}, who is married, leaving a hotel with a woman who is not his wife. {T} saw him see it. Neither of them said anything. Now {T}'s wife has invited {J} and {P} for dinner.
scenarios.prompt: You know a teammate's secret.

choices.label: Talk to {T} privately
choices.desc: Tell him you won't lie for him.
choices.text: {T} begs him to keep quiet. {J} says he won't tell, and won't lie either. The dinner is the longest of his life.

choices.label: Decline the dinner
choices.text: He finds an excuse. {P} asks why. He changes the subject, badly.

choices.label: Tell {P}
choices.hint: Your partner may not keep it.
choices.text: {P} is horrified, and now they both have to pretend at dinner. She's better at it than he is.

scenarios.title: The Team Photo
scenarios.text: Official team photo day. The photographer is putting players in rows by height and fame. {J} has been put at the end of the back row, half cut out of the frame.
scenarios.prompt: Your place in the team photo.

choices.label: Accept your spot
choices.text: He stands at the end with a grin. Next year, he promises himself, the middle.

choices.label: Photobomb it
choices.text: The official photo goes to print with {J} giving the captain rabbit ears. The club uses it on the calendar anyway.

scenarios.title: The Senior Players' Meeting
scenarios.text: The senior players have been asked to meet the board about the club's direction. Someone has to speak for the squad. All eyes turn to {J}.
scenarios.prompt: Speak for the squad?

choices.label: Speak up for everyone
choices.hint: Respect from the squad. Notice from the board.
choices.text: He speaks clearly and calmly. The board agrees to fix the training pitches and pay bonuses on time. The squad cheers when he walks back in.

choices.label: Let someone else speak
choices.text: {CAP} speaks. {J} nods along.
